statement: Whenever find_anagrams(s,p) returns a result r, r is a duplicate-free list whose entries are exactly the valid start indices: for every integer i with -2^63 <= i < 2^63, i occurs in r if and only if 0 <= i and i + len(p) <= len(s) and the contiguous substring of s of length len(p) starting at i, namely s[i], s[i+1], ..., s[i+len(p)-1], is an anagram of p. Here anagram of p means that the substring has length len(p) and for every byte c the number of positions j in the substring with value c equals the number of positions j in p with p[j]=c; duplicate-free means for all k,k' with 0 <= k < len(r) and 0 <= k' < len(r), r[k]=r[k'] implies k=k'; and i occurs in r means there exists k with 0 <= k < len(r) and r[k]=i.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 30000, 1 <= len(p) <= 30000, all bytes of s and p are in the range 97..122 (lowercase ASCII letters).

statement: For every s and p satisfying the preconditions, find_anagrams(s,p) returns a result (there exists a vector v such that the call evaluates to ok v); it does not fail, overflow, or panic.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 30000, 1 <= len(p) <= 30000, all bytes of s and p are in the range 97..122.

statement: Whenever find_anagrams(s,p) returns r, for every j with 0 <= j < len(r), if 0 <= r[j] and r[j] + len(p) <= len(s), then the contiguous substring of s of length len(p) starting at r[j] is an anagram of p (same length and same multiset of bytes as p).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 30000, 1 <= len(p) <= 30000, all bytes of s and p are in the range 97..122.

statement: Whenever find_anagrams(s,p) returns r, every entry r[j] with 0 <= j < len(r) satisfies 0 <= r[j] and r[j] + len(p) <= len(s).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 30000, 1 <= len(p) <= 30000, all bytes of s and p are in the range 97..122.

statement: Whenever find_anagrams(s,p) returns r, for every integer i with 0 <= i and i + len(p) <= len(s), if the contiguous substring of s of length len(p) starting at i is an anagram of p, then i occurs in r (there exists k with 0 <= k < len(r) and r[k]=i).
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 30000, 1 <= len(p) <= 30000, all bytes of s and p are in the range 97..122.

statement: Whenever find_anagrams(s,p) returns r, the entries of r are pairwise distinct: for all k,k' with 0 <= k < len(r) and 0 <= k' < len(r), if r[k]=r[k'] then k=k'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 30000, 1 <= len(p) <= 30000, all bytes of s and p are in the range 97..122.

statement: Whenever find_anagrams(s,p) returns r, if len(p) <= len(s) then len(r) <= len(s)-len(p)+1; and if len(p) > len(s) then len(r)=0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 30000, 1 <= len(p) <= 30000, all bytes of s and p are in the range 97..122.

statement: For every byte string q such that len(q)=len(p) and for every byte c the number of positions j with q[j]=c equals the number of positions j with p[j]=c, if find_anagrams(s,p) returns r and find_anagrams(s,q) returns r', then for every integer i with -2^63 <= i < 2^63, i occurs in r if and only if i occurs in r'.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 30000, 1 <= len(p) <= 30000, all bytes of s and p are in the range 97..122.

statement: Whenever find_anagrams(s,p) returns r, len(r) > 0 if and only if there exists an integer i with 0 <= i and i + len(p) <= len(s) such that the contiguous substring of s of length len(p) starting at i is an anagram of p.
preconditions: 1 <= len(s) <= 30000, 1 <= len(p) <= 30000, all bytes of s and p are in the range 97..122.
